findings.impact: The green reruns prove bounded scout execution, not strong independent layer claim.
findings.required_repair: Keep stronger claim language blocked until a layer-specific lift artifact moves a layer beyond formal_scout with explicit consumer eligibility.
findings.title: Current layer receipts remain formal_scout rows with promotion_allowed=false.

findings.impact: Shared plumbing is allowed, but it increases label-drift risk: layer identity can become configuration text unless the common runner has layer-specific math and non-vacuous per-layer ablations.
findings.required_repair: Add or verify per-layer implementation sections for each layer, and make validators require layer-specific source hooks/witnesses instead of wrapper presence alone.
findings.title: Many per-layer files are wrappers over shared runners rather than layer-local implementations.

findings.impact: This misses the source-native runtime requirement for per-row spinor phase gradients and leaves the PyTorch tool-depth packet genuinely open.
findings.required_repair: Run tool_depth_pytorch_autograd_per_row_spinor_phase before calling any layer gradient-capable.
findings.title: PyTorch is used for tensors/spinors, but autograd/gradient maps are absent from the active layer runners.

findings.impact: Validators accepted these rows, but a stricter strong-claim standard should require explicit per-tool ablation fields and measured deltas for every load-bearing tool.
findings.required_repair: Tighten the validator or repair those receipts so tool_ablations and ablation_outcome_delta both exist and agree.
findings.title: Some receipts rely on ablation_outcome_delta without a tool_ablations field.

findings.impact: Duplicates are not automatically wrong, but they are exactly the pattern that can make labels look like separate layer sims when the measured dynamics are the same.
findings.required_repair: Add a layer-distinctiveness gate: same-source shared plumbing may pass only if each layer has a required unique witness and at least one layer-specific control gap absent from sibling layers.
findings.title: Duplicate numeric signatures across different layers suggest shared-scaffold leakage or insufficient layer-specific separation.

findings.impact: A layer can run over candidate geometry surfaces, but it is still not situated inside a chosen G-structure.
findings.required_repair: Run deeper standalone G-structure choice and embedding criteria after tool-depth packets; keep layer embedding locked until a separate gate passes.
findings.title: Standalone geometry/G-candidate scouts exist; G-structure choice and layer embedding remain locked.

findings.impact: The project already knew these were missing; the green layer reruns should not have overridden this queue.
findings.required_repair: Continue the tool-depth queue in order, beginning with tool_depth_pytorch_autograd_per_row_spinor_phase.
findings.title: The current repair matrix explicitly says deeper per-tool packets remain open.

findings.impact: Von Neumann/Renyi/MI/conditional/coherent/log-negativity-style readouts are present where emitted, but this does not yet test every relevant entropy pattern across every layer, G-candidate, and perturbation/control family.
findings.required_repair: Create an entropy-variant packet after carrier/tool depth is stronger, keeping entropy as derived readout rather than primary object.
findings.title: QIT entropy readouts exist, but the current layer set is not an exhaustive entropy-variant campaign.

main_verdict: The layer receipts run and pass as bounded formal scouts, but they are still bounded scouts and do not have promotion admission yet. The deeper audit found real missing work: autograd gradients, PEPS contraction-depth, true G-structure selection/embedding, stricter per-tool ablations, and layer-distinctiveness gates.
